messages:
Alejandra (infra): heads-up: yesterday 02:14 UTC we had a ~2h capacity squeeze in apac that pushed several inference pods to near‑OOM and triggered request throttles. root cause sketch below, pls chime in.

Sam (eng-runtime): saw the alerts. metric spike was GPU memory pressure + per-node queue depth. lots of long-seq chat sessions from a single customer org.

Ryan (oncall): timeline: 02:10 queue latency started climbing -> 02:12 GPU mem pressure event -> 02:15 autoscaler attempted scale up -> 02:22 scale up effective (node join). during 02:12-02:22 we shed some requests and ran fallbacks.

Maria (prod-forecasting): note: we had a 14% forecast miss for APAC evening window due to a promotional send from Partner X (Priya pls confirm). this was outside our usual seasonal uplift.

Priya (sales): yep, partner ran an uncoordinated campaign at 02:00 local. they used long-context bot sessions (20k token histories) for a demo. they didn't opt into Dedicated.

Leon (sre): observations: KV cache grew 3x per-session for those long chats; this doubled per-req memory on the GPU runtime. combined with medium batch settings we hit an OOM threshold on several P4d pods.

Sam (eng-runtime): concrete evidence in logs: 
```
runtime: alloc_gpu_mem failed 0x7ff.. at seq_len 20480, kv_size 3.1G
batcher: queued 48 requests, avg_seq_len 17840
```
We were running kernel path A (fallback) which uses slightly more memory than quantized path B.

Alejandra (infra): autoscaler behavior: it scales by pod count but we hit AZ instance quota in apac-1 which prevented faster node adds. AutoScaleBot shows repeat failures: 
- 02:14 request for 6 x a100 instances -> quota error
- 02:18 fallback to smaller instance type (slower) -> join 02:22

AutoScaleBot: Scaling event: requested 6 a100 -> failed (quota) -> requested 8 v100_alt -> partial success (4 added) at 02:22.

Ryan (oncall): consequence: throttles for premium customers and degraded latencies. We routed to fallbacks which increased token cost by ~12% for the affected window.

Sam (eng-runtime): immediate mitigations we ran: lowered batch size on apac pool, enabled kv-eviction aggressive policy for sessions > 6k tokens, and forced model-variant fallback to a quantized model for noisy tenant IDs.

Leon (sre): short-term actions to prevent recurrence:
- add per-tenant concurrency cap (soft limit) and circuit-breaker for extreme seq_len
- add mem-pressure alert at 65% (we had only 85% previously)
- create pre-warm path for largest instances to avoid AZ quota slowdowns (warm-up quota request)

Maria (prod-forecasting): longer-term: update forecasting model to include partner marketing calendar spikes, and add a "large-session" multiplier for token-ageing traffic. also adding a prediction-based buffer for apac evening windows (+20% until model proven).

Priya (sales): will coordinate partner comms and require advance notice for demo runs > 10k token avg.

Alejandra (infra): cost discussion: fallback quantized model increased CPU usage on host and some extra routing; estimated extra cost ~ $1.8k over the 2h window. we should track cost per mitigation.

Sam (eng-runtime): follow-ups (tickets):
- T1: implement per-tenant seq_len gating + circuit-breaker (ENG-RUNTIME-324)
- T2: autoscaler: surface quota-errors into ops dashboard + runbook (INFRA-ops-211)
- T3: forecasting: add partner calendar field and large-session feature (DATA-forecast-58)
- T4: create producer-facing doc for session limits and suggested client-side keying (DOCS-89)

Leon (sre): retro notes: what surprised us -> KV cache growth was the primary multiplier (not raw QPS). that means caching heuristics need more defensive defaults.

Ryan (oncall): recommend we add a synthetic test that opens a fleet of long-session streams at low QPS to exercise KV growth without inflating normal forecasts.

Alejandra (infra): agreed. action owners: Sam->T1/T4, Maria->T3, Leon->T2, Priya->partner comms. I'll file a post-incident capacity purchase request to prep apac-1 for the next 6 weeks.

Priya (sales): pinging partner now. thanks everyone. :pray:

Sam (eng-runtime): thanks. I'll push a small runtime change to lower default batch_size in apac for 2 weeks as a stopgap.

Alejandra (infra): closing note: we avoided hard OOM crashes thanks to fallbacks; main learning is to treat long-session token churn as its own traffic class. will schedule a 30min deep-dive this Friday.
